About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for startups. Open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

The Role

Rho is hiring Design Technologists — people who design products by building them. You lead with taste and user intuition, but you work in the medium: prototyping in code, leveraging AI tools, getting to real signal before anyone's written a PRD. You're not waiting for requirements. You're generating them.

The design role has more leverage than it's ever had. AI is compressing the space between insight and artifact. A designer who can prototype in code, think in systems, and build deep customer intuition can now shape product in ways that weren't possible two years ago. This role exists to capture that.

Know the customer. Build real expertise in how founders and early-stage companies manage money. Use research when it's right, but also trust the pattern recognition that comes from sustained proximity to the problem.

Set product direction. Your design judgment is a strategic input, not a downstream service. Shape what gets built, what gets cut, and what gets rethought. Bring clarity to ambiguity. Say no to the right things.

title: Staff Product Designer
description:
Hi! 👋 I'm Chris, head of Product Design at Ashby.

We're looking for a versatile, intrinsically motivated designer who is excited to contribute to rethinking how modern software is designed. At Ashby, you'll be part designer, part product manager, part consultant, and part design system manager (or some combination of the 4!). We do design differently here, and if that excites you, read on.

Our unique approach is working - we're growing >100% year-over-year and have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, very low churn, and many years of runway. We're backed by amazing investors like Y Combinator, Elad Gil, Lachy Groom, and many more! We’ll share more details once we meet.

How We Work

In my previous roles, product teams always consisted of a product manager, a designer, and ~4-5 engineers. This may sound familiar to you! The product manager briefs the designer who then designs. After designing, mocks are handed to the engineers.

We take a more principled approach here at Ashby. If you've been designing software enough, you'll realize in actuality, design is required in varying degrees on each project. Sometimes in the past, I'd be asked to design yet another settings page, when really all that was needed was an engineer to reuse existing components and just follow some documentation I had written. Other times, I felt I should effectively be the product manager and own a project from beginning to end. In these latter cases, it made sense that I was even the one providing project updates and managing resources rather than constantly being pinged by a separate product manager.

This principled approach is now what we do here, and it is part of what has allowed Ashby to take down incumbents in multiple verticals all at once. We don't settle for the status quo—we actively resist reversion to the mean.

Currently, I report to Benji, the co-founder & CEO. Both Abhik and Benji (our founders) care deeply about design, which at first glance may seem counterintuitive given the number of full-time designers that we employ. The belief is not that design is unimportant, but rather that it should be owned by the product team collectively, not solely by a group of full-time designers who happen to have the job title.

The design department’s job at Ashby is not to make every single design decision but to equip our entire product team to make better decisions themselves, as well as edit decisions that PMs/Engineers choose to make. That, while tackling the biggest design challenges ourselves.

Separate from design, you may also be excited by the fact that we maintain a near seed-stage-like culture with fuzzy lines between functional roles, as much autonomy as you can handle, and a focus on IC-work with an almost-no-meeting culture. title: Senior Product Designer
description:
We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer who can shape how internal communicators experience Workshop — and help define what it looks like when great design meets AI. This isn’t a role where you execute a spec and hand it off. You’ll work across the full arc of a product problem, from the fuzzy early stages to polished final experiences, and you’ll bring other designers along with you as you go.

You’ll be one of the people who helps us figure out what AI-assisted design looks like in practice — not as a buzzword, but as a genuine tool for making better products, faster. You’re curious about it, experimenting with it, and excited to push the team forward on it.

This role reports to the Head of Product Design. It has no direct reports today, but mentorship and team leadership are a real part of the job.

This is a hybrid role based in Omaha, Nebraska.

As The Senior Product Designer, You Will



- Own design projects end-to-end — from early discovery and fuzzy problem framing through final delivery and iteration
- Collaborate closely with product, engineering, and cross-functional stakeholders to solve real, meaningful problems — not just make things look good
- Apply AI to your own workflow and to the products you’re designing, and help the rest of the design team do the same
- Mentor and support other designers, giving them honest feedback, modeling good process, and helping them grow their confidence and craft
- Hold both the detail and the system at once — sweating the UI while also thinking about patterns, consistency, and product strategy
- Contribute to a design culture worth being part of: thoughtful critiques, useful documentation, and a bias toward learning out loud

To be successful in this role, you’ll need to:



- Have 4+ years of product design experience, with meaningful time in a senior or lead capacity
- Show your work — a portfolio that demonstrates clear thinking, strong taste, and impact that you can actually speak to
- Be genuinely curious about AI: experimenting with it, learning from it, and helping others do the same — not just nodding along to the trend
- Move fluidly between detailed UI craft and higher-level product and systems thinking without losing the thread
- Communicate clearly and collaborate openly — you know how to work with engineers and PMs in a way that feels like partnership, not handoff

Bonus Points If You



- Have worked at a startup or agency and know what it means to ship in a fast, resource-constrained environment
- Have experience with AI products or B2B SaaS
- Have opinions about where AI is taking design — and can back them up with something more than vibes
- Have helped non-designers understand and use design systems, AI tools, or new workflows
- Bring a little delight into the work 🙂

Compensation And Benefits



- Hybrid role based in Omaha, Nebraska
- Competitive total compensation
- Stock options
- Healthcare
- 401(k)
- Unlimited vacation
- Flexible work environment

A career in IBM Software means you’ll be leading the teams that transform our customers’ challenges into world-class solutions.

You will be leading a design team dedicated to HashiCorp’s industry-leading suite of security products. As the standard for cloud infrastructure automation, HashiCorp products (like Vault and Boundary) are critical to the world’s largest organizations.
